key_insight: A privacy-preserving Llama 3.3 70B pipeline extracted oncology registry variables with high F1 scores without task-specific fine-tuning.
clinical_relevance: The approach could reduce manual registry abstraction workload while keeping identifiable patient data within hospital infrastructure.
method: Processed 6,700 oncology notes at a Singapore cancer centre to extract over 50 variables.
Used local Hide-In-Plain-Sight de-identification before LLM extraction.
Evaluated outputs as correct, missing, spurious, or incorrect against adjudicated reference data.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on 200 randomly sampled notes yielded F1 scores of 97.2% for diagnosis, 95.8% for histology, 92.6% for stage, 91.4% for biomarkers, and 88.1% for treatments.
watch_item: External testing was preliminary, involving only 50 notes, and showed reduced performance for list-valued variables.
paper_title: Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model Deployment for Oncology Registry Abstraction: Structure-Aware Evaluation in a Real-World Clinical Setting
